# Fixture Builders

Reads a Go struct definition, emits a fluent builder with
one `With*` setter per exported field.

## go:generate directive

```go
//go:generate testkit builder -o storetest/user_builder.gen.go User
//go:generate testkit builder -o storetest/item_builder.gen.go Item

// Multiple structs into one file:
//go:generate testkit builder -o storetest/builders.gen.go User Item
```

## Default output

`<package>test/<subject>_builder.gen.go`

## What is generated

Given a struct `User` with fields `ID`,
`Name`, `Role`:

```go
// Code generated by testkit builder. DO NOT EDIT.

package storetest

import "example.com/myapp/store"

// UserBuilder constructs store.User
// values for tests. Start with NewUserBuilder,
// override fields with With* setters, call Build.
type UserBuilder struct {
    v store.User
}

// NewUserBuilder creates a builder seeded with
// defaults. The caller provides sensible defaults; the builder
// provides fluent overrides.
func NewUserBuilder(
    defaults store.User,
) *UserBuilder {
    return &UserBuilder{v: defaults}
}

func (b *UserBuilder) WithID(v string) *UserBuilder {
    b.v.ID = v
    return b
}

func (b *UserBuilder) WithName(v string) *UserBuilder {
    b.v.Name = v
    return b
}

func (b *UserBuilder) WithRole(v string) *UserBuilder {
    b.v.Role = v
    return b
}

// ... one With* per exported field

func (b *UserBuilder) Build() store.User {
    return b.v
}
```

## Injection point

The developer writes a hand-written constructor that wraps
the generated one with sensible domain defaults:

```go
// storetest/fixtures.go — hand-written

func NewUser() *UserBuilder {
    return NewUserBuilder(store.User{
        ID:   "test-user",
        Name: "Alice",
        Role: "admin",
    })
}
```

Tests then override only the fields relevant to their
assertion:

```go
u := storetest.NewUser().
    WithName("Bob").
    Build()
```

## Nested structs

Fields that are themselves structs get a `With*` that
takes the entire nested value. If the nested type also has
a generated builder, call sites compose:

```go
u := storetest.NewUser().
    WithAddress(
        addresstest.NewAddress().
            WithCity("London").
            Build(),
    ).
    Build()
```

## Why

Builder patterns eliminate brittle inline struct
construction in tests. When a field is added to a
production struct, only the hand-written defaults
constructor needs updating — every test that uses the
builder continues to compile and run without modification.

Without builders:

```go
// Breaks when a new required field is added to User.
u := store.User{
    ID: "test", Name: "Alice", Role: "admin",
}
```

## Generated tests

For every builder, a companion test file is generated
(e.g., `user_builder.gen_test.go`). These
tests verify every `With*` setter and the `Build` method.

```go
// Code generated by testkit builder. DO NOT EDIT.

package storetest_test

import (
    "testing"

    "go.thesmos.sh/testkit"
    "example.com/myapp/store"
    "example.com/myapp/store/storetest"
)

func TestUserBuilder_Defaults(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()

    defaults := store.User{
        ID:   "default-id",
        Name: "Alice",
    }

    got := storetest.NewUserBuilder(defaults).Build()
    testkit.Equal(t, got, defaults,
        "Build without setters must return defaults unchanged")
}

func TestUserBuilder_WithID(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()

    defaults := store.User{ID: "original"}
    got := storetest.NewUserBuilder(defaults).
        WithID("overridden").
        Build()

    testkit.Equal(t, got.ID, "overridden",
        "WithID must set ID")
}

func TestUserBuilder_WithName(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()

    got := storetest.NewUserBuilder(store.User{}).
        WithName("Bob").
        Build()

    testkit.Equal(t, got.Name, "Bob",
        "WithName must set Name")
}

// ... one test per With* setter

func TestUserBuilder_IndependentBuilds(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()

    b := storetest.NewUserBuilder(store.User{})

    a := b.WithID("a").Build()
    // Builder is consumed — create a new one for b.
    bVal := storetest.NewUserBuilder(store.User{}).
        WithID("b").Build()

    testkit.NotEqual(t, a.ID, bVal.ID,
        "independent builds must not alias")
}
```

The generated tests use zero-value defaults and simple
scalar overrides — no domain knowledge needed. Coverage
target: 100% of the generated builder code.

## Scale

33 existing files, 275 `With*` methods = ~2,200 lines generated.
33 companion test files x ~(10 + N_fields*8) lines = ~2,500 lines generated.
